_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). TOP-RIGHT CORNER OF THE SCROLL, and it is 62% EMPTY SILK. The upper two thirds carry no landscape at all: the seal-script title 葛稚川移居圖 runs down x 0.60-0.82 and a running-script colophon down x 0.11-0.55, both floating on bare silk. Calligraphy is ink on nothing -- it is not rock, not foliage, and any mask that reaches above y 0.62 has failed. The landscape is a single band along the bottom edge, and it is DISTANT: peaks seen across a gulf of air, drawn small. There is no near canopy anywhere in this tile, no trunk thicker than a hair, and no 夾葉 outlined leaves. The only real foliage is 遠樹 -- distant-tree convention: a dark dabbed crown about 15-30 tile px across, one or two thin vertical trunk strokes under it, often a pale blue-green (石綠) wash smeared behind the row. Four such rows exist and they are the four tree objects below. EVERYTHING ELSE IN THE BAND IS STONE, and this tile is where the colour-only pass would have gone wrong, because the whole band is a similar mid-grey. Three decoys to know by name: (1) the sharp central peak at x 0.38-0.60 wears a heavy cap of 点苔 moss dots on its crest and left shoulder -- dots on stone, dense and round, no crown silhouette, no trunk, kind:rock; (2) the great pale flank sweeping in from the top-right corner (x 0.70-1.0) is built from long parallel 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre strokes that fan downhill, and at thumbnail size the fan reads as a spray of pine needles -- there is not one leaf glyph in it; (3) the wooded slopes on the left (x 0.08-0.48, y 0.73-1.0) are genuinely half foliage and half rock, dab-texture and hemp-fibre interleaved on the same slope, so their boxes are SEARCH REGIONS and must be refined per-pixel, never used raw. The treeline at x 0-0.19 on the top-left crest is the cleanest tree object here: crowns silhouetted against empty silk with visible trunks, and it is the only box in this tile with a clean edge. All content continues off the bottom edge into t007 and off the left edge into t002.

objects.name: row of distant trees on the top-left ridge crest
objects.note: the cleanest foliage in the tile. Six or seven small crowns of dabbed leaf dots standing on a crest, each with a thin vertical trunk stroke beneath it, silhouetted against bare silk above -- so the top edge of the mask is unambiguous. A pale blue-green wash lies behind the row. The lower quarter of this box is the crest rock the trees stand on; clip the mask at the trunk feet

objects.name: wooded ridge slope below the crest treeline
objects.note: SEARCH REGION, NOT A TIGHT BOX. The treeline continues down-right along the falling ridge, but here the crowns merge into a continuous dab texture laid over the ridge's own moss dotting and hemp-fibre strokes. Roughly half these pixels are stone. Individual trunks are still findable around x 0.17-0.19, y 0.815-0.85. A per-pixel pass must keep only the crown clusters and the blue-green wash; using this box raw is exactly how the rock got animated last time

objects.name: wooded slope along the bottom-left edge
objects.note: SEARCH REGION. Same texture as wooded-slope-upper-left, denser and darker, clipped by the bottom edge and continuing into t007. Recognisable tree silhouettes with trunks around x 0.20-0.33, y 0.90-0.98; the rest is dab-on-stone. Highest rock contamination of any foliage box in this tile

objects.name: row of distant trees on the middle ridge, right of the peak
objects.note: a short row of four or five crowns on a crest with a blue-green wash pooled under them, and at least three thin trunks visible descending at x 0.593, 0.615 and 0.63. Left and right of this box the same crest carries only moss dots -- do not widen it, the dots are not leaves

objects.name: three individual trees on the right ridge line
objects.note: three separate little trees marching down the ridge line, each an isolated dark crown on a clearly drawn short trunk, standing on open pale rock -- the most unambiguous wood/leaf pairing in the tile despite being the smallest. Each tree alone is far below the size floor; they are boxed together as one band and should animate as one soft group, not individually

objects.name: sharp pointed peak, centre
objects.note: DECOY. The dominant silhouette of the band, and its crest and left shoulder are capped with dense 点苔 moss dotting that at thumbnail size reads as a treed summit. Up close the dots sit flat on the stone in chains that follow the contour -- no crown silhouettes break the skyline, no trunks. kind:rock, NEVER animate. The peak's body below the cap is plain hemp-fibre stroke

objects.name: rock ridge under the middle treeline
objects.note: the stone that treeline-mid-ridge-crest stands on, plus a dark moss-dotted cap at x 0.735-0.79, y 0.775-0.815 that is too small to box separately and is pure dotting on stone. Runs off the bottom edge

objects.name: great pale flank sweeping in from the top-right corner
objects.note: DECOY, and the largest single surface in the band. A smooth pale slope drawn with long parallel 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre lines that fan downhill; the fan mimics a spray of pine needles at any reduced size. There is no branch and no trunk in it. The slope's upper-left boundary runs diagonally from about (0.95,0.64) down to (0.72,1.0), so the upper-left triangle of this box is bare silk. The three trees of ridge-trees-right-flank sit ON this slope and are the only animatable pixels inside these bounds

objects.name: pale ridge body under the left treeline
objects.note: the crest and falling flank that treeline-crest-far-left stands on, fading into mist at the bottom left. Faint hemp-fibre stroke, a few contour dots. Rigid

objects.name: empty silk carrying the title and colophon
objects.note: 62% of the tile. Untouched silk apart from two blocks of calligraphy: the seal-script title 葛稚川移居圖 down x 0.60-0.82, y 0.22-0.68, and a running-script colophon down x 0.11-0.55, y 0.25-0.72. Both are dense black ink and WILL be picked up by any darkness-based foliage detector -- they are writing, they are flat, and they must never move. Two caveats on this box: the last two colophon characters hang BELOW it, down to about y 0.72 at x 0.19-0.33, over bare silk that no other box covers; and the top-right rock flank intrudes above y 0.62 from about x 0.95
